newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-MOYA BEATS GOELLNER TO PUT SPAIN AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MOYA BEATS GOELLNER TO PUT SPAIN AHEAD.

text.p: Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya scored a straight-sets victory over Marc Goellner to give Spain a 1-0 lead over Germany in their Davis Cup world group first round tie on Friday.
Moya, making his first appearance in Spain since reaching the Melbourne final, settled more quickly than his opponent and ran out a 6-4 6-3 6-3 winner in one hour 40 minutes.
"It wasn't easy to win this first match, especially after all the euphoria in Australia," said Moya, who broke Goellner twice to lead 5-2 in the first set.
The German broke back to 5-4 but Moya held his serve and hit two aces in one game as he took control of the match.
"After taking the first set I had more and more confidence," said Moya.
The Spaniard came to the net repeatedly and produced several winning drop-shots as he outmanouevered the German, who never seemed to settle on a clay court constructed especially for the event.
Fans of both sides made their presence felt.
One group of German supporters carried a banner reading "Who is Moya?".
Another banner remembered the great absentees from the tie.
"Davis Cup (possible) without Becker and Stich," said a banner written in German. Both Boris Becker and Michael Stich decided against playing the tie.
Albert Costa and Hendrik Dreekman were playing in Friday's second singles.
